title: fixtures-vibes runtime profile
description: Data a runtime supplies so the shared compliance suite can start, reach and reset it. Profiles carry no assertions and no scenario-specific branching.

runtime.description: Stable runtime name, e.g. piclaw, gi, vibes-python, vibes-go, tau-prime.

version.description: Runtime commit or release under test.

lifecycle.description: Shell commands run by the suite. Each receives FIXTURES_ROOT (fresh temp dir), FIXTURES_PORT, FIXTURE_MODEL_URL (OpenAI-compatible base URL), FIXTURE_MODEL_ID.

prepare.description: Create fresh store/workspace/config under FIXTURES_ROOT pointing the model provider at FIXTURE_MODEL_URL.

start.description: Start the server in the foreground; the suite owns the process.

reset.description: Optional: restore a clean state between scenarios without restarting. Default: stop, prepare, start.

session.description: How the suite reaches a usable chat session through the runtime's public interface.

idField.description: JSON pointer-ish dotted path to the new session id in the response.

open.description: URL path template to open a session, e.g. '/' or '/?session={id}'.

capabilities.description: Capabilities from capabilities.json this runtime claims. Scenarios requiring an unclaimed capability must appear in the skips file.

skips.description: Path (relative to the profile) of the skips file.

selectors.description: Only where markup cannot match the canonical role/name selector. Keys are canonical selector names from the suite.

routes.description: Only for HTTP routes the suite must call directly (seeding through public API). Keys are canonical route names.

external.description: Already-running instance (e.g. the shared Piclaw reference). The suite cannot restart it, so isolation uses fresh sessions and model reset only when the instance is idle.

tools.description: Optional map from canonical tool names used by specs to the runtime's tool names. 'shell' runs a POSIX shell command with a 'command' string argument (default 'bash'). 'activate', when set, names a tool taking {"names": [...]} that must be called before using tools that are not active by default.

button.description: Regular expression for the accessible name of the control that approves a pending fixture tool call, e.g. '^Allow '.

approval.description: Opt-in for runtimes whose tool calls always wait for user approval and cannot be pre-approved by configuration. The suite clicks the matching control whenever it appears.

setAgentAvatar.description: Composer text that sets the agent avatar; {source} is replaced by a data:image/png;base64 URL.

clearAgentAvatar.description: Composer text that restores the default agent avatar.

selectModel.description: Composer text of the native model command; {model} is replaced by a fixture model ID (fixture-1, fixture-2) or by an unknown ID.

commands.description: Composer commands the suite types to seed runtime settings that have no shared API, or that a scenario exercises. Required for the capabilities that use them (@cap-agent-avatar: setAgentAvatar/clearAgentAvatar; @cap-compaction: selectModel).

path.description: Regular expression for the URL path of rate-limited writes.

perMinute.description: Maximum matching writes per sliding minute.

rateLimit.description: Pace browser writes to a known rate limit instead of hitting it; rate limits are not under test.

when.description: Case-insensitive regex that identifies the runtime's summary requests to the model (matched against system and user text).

summaries.description: Reply text for each summary request of one compaction, in order, in the format the runtime accepts. A literal \\n is a newline.

compaction.description: How the fixture model answers this runtime's compaction summary requests (@cap-compaction). Defaults to one plain summary for any request.
